recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13872 unless OO later reopens the broader Observation.component guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-13872 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request for STU3 asking for additional examples to clarify when to use Observation.component versus separate related Observations: a newborn Apgar score as one Observation with five components, and BMI as a case where height and weight should remain separate observations.
initial_application: Historical commit 9b52190635e745d4a09b61888e3a47a9ed9aa05b added the Apgar and BMI component guidance to source/observation/observation-notes.xml. Its subject appears to have transposed GForge issue numbers, but the patch contents match the FHIR-13872 Jira request.
additional_context: Observation is active in source/fhir.ini. The current notes have been refactored from STU3 Observation.related terminology to current Observation.hasMember and Observation.derivedFrom terminology. Related FHIR-14392 added broader component guidance to the same section, and later FHIR-51724 resolved no-change because the current component/hasMember distinction was already clarified. A 2021 Zulip implementers thread quoted the same Apgar and BMI guidance as current R4 component guidance; direct issue-key Zulip and Confluence searches did not find conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/observation/observation-notes.xml already says Observation.component is for supporting results that cannot reasonably be interpreted outside the parent Observation, lists a newborn Apgar score as one Observation with five components, and says BMI should not contain height and weight components because those measurements are clinically relevant observations on their own.
